papers.summary: Environmental monitoring is crucial for addressing challenges related to climate change,water resource management, and disaster risk mitigation. This study advances the application of machine learning techniques for anomaly detection and forecasting of temperature and groundwater, focusing on temperature anomalies in Ticino, Switzerland, and groundwater level (GWL) fluctuations in Mendatica and Triora, Italy. By integrating these two domains, this research develops a scalable and accurate approach to enhance real-time environmental monitoring. Hydrometeorological data often exhibit complex, non-linear relationships that conventional statistical models struggle to capture. This study employs advanced machine learning models, including Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and the Prophet model,to enhance real-time anomaly detection and forecasting. Additionally, statistical models and machine learning models such as Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA),Seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Recurrent Nerural Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (RNN-GRU) are utilized to provide a comparative assessment of traditional forecasting techniques against machine learning-based approaches. The methodological framework significantly improves predictive capabilities, with broad applications in disaster preparedness, water resource management, and climate change adaptation. The research methodology follows a structured approach, beginning with data collection from temperature sensors in Ticino, and piezometers in Mendatica and Triora. The acquired data undergo preprocessing to remove inconsistencies, ensuring high-quality input for analysis. A machine learning-driven anomaly detection framework is implemented to identify outliers in time-series data. papers.title: From the mountains to the sky: Aerial Cable-Cars lifting social inclusion and transport equity in Latin America
papers.summary: Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) is a region with deep transport and spatial inequalities, producing differences in travel behaviour and transport supply across communities, as people living in the peripheries experience longer travel times and costs to access essential amenities. Topography is another important factor exacerbating these inequalities, as many LAC settlements are located near the Andes Mountains. Disadvantaged communities (DC) in the region are usually located in hilly terrain, often in areas at risk of landslides, and are characterised by informal development. In this context, Aerial Cable-Cars (ACC) presents a mode of public transport that provides high-quality service and infrastructure in LAC cities with the potential to improve social inclusion and accessibility for vulnerable communities. ACC have been rapidly adopted throughout LAC since their first introduction in Medellín in 2004. And particularly after 2010, when more than 90% of operational ACCs were inaugurated. This thesis seeks to contribute to the understanding of ACC technology as a mode of transport in LAC urban settlements, along with its implications for activity participation and transport-related social exclusion (TRSE), accessibility and transport equity, and mode choice. To do so, the study first conducted a literature review of empirical evidence on ACC transport projects in LAC. Then, the thesis focused on two case studies in Colombia: Bogotá and Manizales. In Bogotá, the first ACC (TransMiCable) was inaugurated in 2018, connecting Ciudad Bolívar’s residents to the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system and primarily serving as a feeder. In Manizales, the ACC system (Cable Aéreo) comprises three interconnected lines, inaugurated in 2009, 2014, and 2025.

papers.title: Research on the Optimized 3D DEM‒SPH Algorithm and Impact Parameters of Surge Wave Amplitude for Granular Landslides
papers.source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.summary: ObjectiveMesh-based and Eulerian-Lagrangian methods cannot adequately simulate large deformations, free-surface fragmentation, and fluid-solid interaction during granular landslide-induced surges. A three-dimensional meshless semi-resolved Discrete Element Method (DEM) and Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) coupling algorithm was developed, incorporating a multiphase flow model to optimize the volume fraction distribution at the coupling interface. The key parameters controlling the maximum surge wave amplitude were systematically investigated to support hazard prediction in reservoir areas.MethodsDEM with a nonlinear contact force model and rolling resistance simulated granular landslides. Each DEM particle obeyed Newton's second law. Normal and tangential contact forces were computed using a nonlinear model with damping. SPH solved the Navier-Stokes equations for the fluid phase using a Wendland C2 kernel with a compact support radius of 2h. A δ‒SPH density diffusion term (coefficient δ=0.1) was added to the continuity equation to reduce pressure noise. The multiphase flow model optimized the volume fraction calculation at the solid-liquid interface using a density-gradient-based control equation. Buoyancy, drag, and reaction forces between DEM and SPH particles were computed using a semi-resolved scheme. Buoyancy was calculated via pressure interpolation from surrounding fluid particles. Drag forces were computed using the Ergun correlation for void fractions below 0.8 and the Wen-Yu correlation for void fractions of 0.8 or above, based on local void fraction and relative velocity. Physical experiments were conducted in a three-dimensional wave tank. The granular landslide material was quartz sand with a mean diameter of 8 mm, density of 2 600 kg/m³, and porosity of 0.23. papers.title: An internally consistent framework for calculating cascading probabilistic earthquake risk and its application to a case study in New Zealand
papers.source: Natural hazards and earth system sciences
papers.summary: Abstract. Quantifying the combined effects of earthquakes and their cascading hazards is essential for realistic risk assessment, yet such approaches remain limited in practice. Dynamic frameworks that explicitly correlate hazard intensities and their uncertainties across cascading perils provide more consistent and physically plausible impact estimates, offering greater value for resilience planning and risk management. This study introduces a probabilistic risk assessment framework that integrates ground shaking, tsunami inundation, liquefaction, landslides, and their combined impacts into a unified modelling approach. The framework employs a fully correlated Monte Carlo–based hazard and damage model, ensuring that secondary perils and their effects on assets are conditionally linked to the triggering ground motions. This dynamic correlation maximises the representation of realistic damage scenarios. The framework was tested in Napier, a city of 65,000 inhabitants situated directly above the Hikurangi Subduction Zone (HSZ), New Zealand’s largest earthquake source with an estimated maximum credible magnitude of about Mw9.1. A 100,000-year stochastic catalogue of ruptures was generated and applied to ~30,000 residential buildings, with ground shaking, tsunami inundation, liquefaction severity, and landslide runouts explicitly modelled. Results include damage state and damage ratio metrics for individual and combined perils. Earthquake shaking and liquefaction emerge as the dominant drivers of risk, followed by tsunami, lateral spreading, and landslides. These findings demonstrate the importance of capturing interdependent hazards in earthquake risk analysis. The framework provides decision makers, urban planners, and the (re)insurance sector with actionable metrics to guide resilience investments, refine underwriting, and minimise losses from cascading hazard events.

Debris flow susceptibility assessment along the G55 expressway in Guangdong Province, China
papers.summary: Western Guangdong Province in China is frequently affected by intense rainfall and related geological hazards, yet studies on debris flow disasters in this area remain limited. In June 2025, four consecutive debris flow events occurred along the Lianzhou-Sanshui section of the G55 Erenhot-Guangzhou Expressway, attracting significant attention. To better understand the spatial distribution and controlling factors of these hazards, this study conducted a debris flow susceptibility assessment for this section. Based on regional topographic, meteorological, and geological conditions, combined with historical disaster data, an evaluation index system and database were established. Four machine learning algorithms, Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were applied and systematically compared. Algorithm performance was assessed using 3-fold spatially independent validation. Among the tested algorithms, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance, with an accuracy of 0.923, recall of 0.879, F1-score of 0.794, and ROC-AUC of 0.927. The debris flow susceptibility was classified into low, medium, and high levels. Medium and high susceptibility areas exhibited clear spatial clustering, mainly in the northern section of the expressway, while the southern section showed generally low susceptibility. Debris flows along the expressway were primarily triggered by shallow surface collapses and landslides that formed cascading hazard chains, while the slipperiness of surface weathering products showed an observed association with debris-flow occurrence and may represent a potential conditioning factor. These findings provide a scientific basis for debris flow risk identification and mitigation and offer insights for improving susceptibility assessment methodologies.

papers.title: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping for Railway Slopes Using Comparative Models and InSAR-Based Validation
papers.summary: Abstract We evaluated landslide susceptibility along the Carajás Railway in Brazil using five approaches: Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting, Multilayer Perceptron, Support Vector Machine, and Weight of Evidence. The models integrated an inventory of 148 landslide events with geomorphological, hydrological, and land-use conditioning factors. We assessed predictive performance using receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve. Random Forest performed best (0.859), followed by Extreme Gradient Boosting (0.850), Multilayer Perceptron (0.687), Weight of Evidence (0.669), and Support Vector Machine (0.459). We independently evaluated susceptibility predictions using ground-deformation time series derived from Sentinel-1 interferometric synthetic aperture radar data processed with the Small Baseline Subset approach. Deformation rates increased progressively across susceptibility classes, with the highest magnitudes concentrated in areas classified as highly susceptible. Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting showed the strongest agreement between susceptibility patterns and observed deformation. The results indicated that interferometric deformation provided an independent physical assessment of susceptibility predictions and strengthened the interpretation of model outputs. The integrated approach improved the reliability of susceptibility assessment and supported risk-informed management of railway slopes.

papers.title: Preliminary Hypothesis About the Polygonal Features Discovered in a Middle Miocene Deep-Sea Sediment Sequence (Kawabata Fm., Hokkaido, Japan)
papers.summary: Numerous landslides occurred in the region of Atsuma (Hokkaido, Japan) as a result of the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi Earthquake. Despite their devastating consequences, the emergence of mass movements has provided a unique opportunity to gain insight into specific chapters of Earth’s history by exposing new natural outcrops and revealing rock strata, including the Middle Miocene Kawabata Formation. The formation primarily comprises sedimentary rocks that reflect various deep-sea environments, especially the continental slope and basin plain of a foreland basin. For this reason, an exposed bedding plane consisting of polygonal features, recently (September 2022) discovered in an outcrop formed at the scarp of a landslide, has aroused interest. Mud cracks or desiccation marks often form in the tidal zone due to exposure to the subaerial environment but not in the aforementioned deep-sea facies. An additional series of evidence of subaerial exposure, with potential wet and dry cycles in a near-shore/coastal environment, was revealed, such as limonite grain coatings and hypocoatings, as well as biotite exfoliation. Based on this evidence, a putative new Middle Miocene facies and a potential new stratigraphic member was proposed in the Kawabata Formation.

papers.title: Deformation and failure mechanism of Jinping landslide in Junlian County, Sichuan Province, China: insight into mineral disintegration characteristics
InSAR observations from multiple tracks reveal rainfall modulation of post-failure reactivation of the Xiongwadashan landslide
papers.summary: Large mountain landslides may remain active after major movement, yet the migration of dominant deformation zones, internal post-failure partitioning, and rainfall modulation remain insufficiently understood. We investigate the Xiongwadashan (XW) landslide on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau using Sentinel-1 LOS observations from selected pre- and post-event periods between 2017 and 2025, terrain-constrained three-dimensional displacement estimates for 2022–2024, CHIRPS rainfall data, and field observations. Before the September 2018 event, deformation was concentrated mainly in the middle–lower slope. After failure, the dominant deformation zone shifted to the middle–upper slope and later extended partially downslope toward the middle slope. Movement was dominated by horizontal, near-downslope displacement, with a peak cumulative east–west displacement of ~ 210 mm at XW1-3. Integrated LOS deformation, three-dimensional displacement, time series, and geomorphic evidence delineated high-deformation, transitional, and low-deformation kinematic zones. The high-deformation zone showed stronger displacement increases following concentrated rainfall, while deformation persisted during relatively low-rainfall periods. These results indicate that rainfall mainly modulated stage-wise acceleration rather than controlling long-term activity, and demonstrate the value of integrating temporal deformation-zone migration with internal kinematic zonation for post-failure landslide monitoring.

papers.title: Integrating Social Innovation and Geoinformatics for Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction: A Sandbox Approach in Mueang Tak District, Thailand
papers.summary: Background and Objectives: Natural disasters, particularly landslides, floods, and droughts, pose increasing threats to the socio-economic stability and environmental security of communities in Mueang Tak District, Tak Province, Thailand. Conventional top-down disaster management strategies often suffer from a critical data-action gap in which advanced spatial technologies and risk information are not effectively translated into locally actionable practices. To address this challenge, this study aimed to integrate social innovation with geoinformatics technology to strengthen community-based disaster risk reduction. The specific objectives were to analyze natural disaster risk areas using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS), investigate community-based social innovation needs, and develop and evaluate “Sandbox Innovation Areas” for landslide, flood, and drought management. Methodology: The study employed an integrated research design structured into four phases: spatial risk assessment, community survey, participatory sandbox development, and evaluation. Spatial data were processed using Google Earth Engine (GEE) and GIS to identify priority risk areas. Social data were collected from 462 residents using stratified multistage cluster random sampling across landslide-prone, flood-prone, and drought-prone areas to assess existing practices and innovation needs. Spatial and social findings were integrated to guide the selection of three pilot sandbox areas and the design of capacity-building activities for Community Innovators. The sandbox process included participatory GIS, field validation, co-creation of community risk maps, and evaluation of perceived knowledge gain and stakeholder opinions. Multisource Information-Based Social Event Detection Using Integrated Deep Neural Architectures and Hybrid Text Representation
papers.summary: Event detection is crucial for timely crisis response, public safety, and combating misinformation by extracting critical signals from real-time social data. The user-generated content on social media platforms has created a critical need for intelligent systems capable of accurately detecting and classifying real-world events across diverse domains. This paper presents a fusion-driven framework for social event detection, leveraging textual data from diverse social media sources and a suite of deep neural architectures to achieve state-of-the-art performance in classifying diverse event categories from noisy, unstructured social media streams. The proposed system collects information from heterogeneous domains, including medical conditions, natural disasters, and sports events, to improve both feature richness and contextual awareness. Our method applies a hybridized deep learning strategy, specifically a customized layered CNN+LSTM architecture. This fusion enables the model to learn spatial and temporal dependencies simultaneously, thus enhancing classification performance. To benchmark effectiveness, we evaluated standalone architectures including CNN, RNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, and BiRNN. Among individual models, LSTM and BiLSTM yielded the top performance, achieving up to 95.3% and 95.8% precision, 95.5% and 96.1% recall, 95.4% and 95.9% accuracy, 95.4% and 96.0% F1-score, 95.6% and 96.2% F1.5, and 95.5% and 96.1% F2-scores, respectively. However, these models still showed variability across event types due to limited contextual generalization from a single-layered perspective. In contrast, the proposed fused CNN and LSTM model recorded promising performance with superior F1-scores on 14 independent classes, achieving 100% on Acne, Earthquake, Landslide, Ringworm, and Vitiligo, 99% on Depression, 98% on Badminton and Tennis, 97% on Cricket, and 96% on FIFA (2022). authors: Pranav Gojare, Vedant Nemade, Arshiya Shaikh
papers.summary: Collapsed buildings, mine roofs and landslides trap people under heavy debris, and their chances of survival fall as time passes. Finding the exact position of a victim is the slowest and riskiest part of collapsed structure search and rescue (CSSR), especially in rural and mining-affected areas where modern equipment, light and stable ground are not available. This paper studies an Advance Body Detection System (ABDS) that sends 1.5 GHz radio-frequency (RF) waves into the debris and uses a low-cost thermal camera to confirm the heat of a human body. The architecture, the RF chain (antenna, VCO, LNA, mixer and analog-to-digital detector), the processing unit and a decision logic that cross-references both sensors are explained with block diagrams, a signal-processing chain and a flowchart, and basic calculations for the RF module and the thermal camera are given. The study, based on recent literature (2020 onwards), shows that RF waves can pass through non-metallic debris and sense the small movement of a hidden person, while a thermal camera detects body heat only at the surface; using both together gives more confident detection than either alone. The main limitations are unwanted reflections from debris, metal and moisture, limited penetration depth, radio-frequency regulations and the need for field trials. No experiments were carried out; calculated values are typical values for explanation

papers.title: Upper bound solution under rainfall-earthquake coupling for curvilinear shallow landslides considering progressive failure mechanism
papers.source: International Conference on Advances in Energy and Environmental Engineering (AEEE)
papers.summary: The shallow landslides are mostly triggered by rainfall and earthquakes. Shallow slopes usually exhibit curved profiles, and obvious multi-stage characteristics are showed in their progressive failure process due to the coupling effect of rainfall and earthquake. Based on the improved upper bound method of limit analysis theory, the stability of curved shallow slopes was analyzed under different coupling conditions of rainfall and earthquakes. A logarithmic spiral sliding surface was proposed for the typical terrain features of steep terrain, and pseudo static seismic effects were corrected to use acceleration amplification coefficients. By the strength and pore water pressure power, the expression was derived for the evolution of the wetting front. Then the energy balance equation was established, four stages of progressive failure mechanisms were revealed. The critical wetting front depth and sliding body length were solved by constructing an allowable velocity field and establishing a variational optimization framework based upon the Euler Lagrange equation. The stability influence of shallow slopes was analyzed depended on effective cohesion, static soil pressure coefficient, and maximum central slope angle. The results indicated that effective cohesion played a key controlling role in the depth of the critical wetting front. The sliding scale was mostly impacted on the static soil pressure coefficient. The maximum central slope angle does not decouple the infiltration process excepted with mainly adjusts the sliding range. These results are good with agree with the values of finite elements method. This study provides a scientific basis for the stability analysis and disaster prevention of curved slopes in mountainous areas.

papers.title: From Fragmented Plans to a Public Regulatory Knowledge Infrastructure: Harmonizing Flood and Landslide Risk Planning in the Central Apennine River Basin District, Italy
papers.summary: Italy’s transition to river basin district governance within the framework of Directive 2000/60/EC unified institutional responsibilities while leaving existing flood and landslide plans in force. District authorities therefore had to integrate instruments with different knowledge bases, classifications and land-use rules. This article examines the integration of nine Hydrogeological Setting Plans (PAIs) into two coordinated plans for the Central Apennine district (42,275 km2), adopted in final form in May 2026. Document analysis compared classifications, intervention conditions and assessment responsibilities, examining 175 public submissions and 118 first-round regional determinations. Geographic information system analysis quantified current classification correspondences and coverage: approximately 1860 km2 within the fluvial planning framework, including safeguard proposals, and 107,045 landslide phenomena occupying approximately 4970 km2. Initial flood transposition retained inherited boundaries, while landslide classification followed a common type–activity matrix. Regulatory comparisons identified conditional extensions of admissibility alongside more selective urban restructuring rules; the plans also established formal updating procedures. Institutional review connected technical choices with regulatory decisions, producing amendments while leaving some precautionary disagreements unresolved. The framework coordinated inherited knowledge without eliminating differences in detail or completeness. The article offers a procedural and regulatory reference for other authorities facing fragmented planning systems; implementation and risk-reduction outcomes require subsequent evaluation.

papers.title: From Reagan to Trump: regional development traps and the remaking of American electoral politics
papers.summary: This paper examines the territorial reconfiguration of American electoral politics since the 1980s, tracing the remaking of Republican support from Reagan’s 1984 landslide to Trump’s three presidential campaigns (2016, 2020, 2024). Drawing on panel data for every presidential election from 1984 to 2024 across 722 commuting zones, we test whether regional development traps, defined as enduring economic underperformance, explain both the shift from Democrats to Republicans and the Republicans’ internal realignment. Mundlak/Correlated Random Effects estimates show backlash is overwhelmingly driven by structural, not cyclical, decline. Short-term economic fluctuations do not predict Republican swing, while long-run territorial position does so decisively. Voters are not responding to recessions. They are registering alienation from an economic order that has failed their communities for a generation. Trump’s gains concentrated in places persistently left behind, whose peripheral position has become entrenched.

papers.title: Road Development in the Tropical Forests of Southeast Asia and the Pacific: A Systematic Review of Forest Loss, Ecological and Health Effects, and Mitigation
papers.summary: Background Road networks in Southeast Asian and Pacific tropical forests are expanding through highways, logging and plantation roads and unmapped access roads. This review synthesized primary evidence on road effects on forest loss, ecology and human health, and evaluated mitigation. Methods Scopus, PubMed and OpenAlex were searched on 7 October 2026 for English-language journal articles published from 2015 (PRISMA 2020). Reviewer 1 and Reviewer 2 independently screened 496 records (κ = 0.94) and assessed 80 full texts (κ = 0.80); the Adjudicator resolved disagreements. Studies were appraised with MMAT 2018, synthesized following SWiM and rated with GRADE-CERQual. Results Sixty-five studies were included, most from Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand; 19 reported forest-loss, 47 ecological and six mitigation outcomes. Forest cover loss was greater nearer roads, at higher road density or length and after construction or completion in nine studies, and no study showed less loss (moderate confidence). Loss extended to 17.7 km with secondary roads in New Guinea (moderate). Structural edge effects reached 34 m at a logging road and 350 m at a highway, whereas soil effects stayed largely on the road surface (moderate). Reptiles or amphibians led roadkill in all seven surveys recording every vertebrate class, and mortality concentrated on short sections near water (moderate). Paved roads reduced crossing by elephants and gibbons and were linked to genetic differentiation in some taxa (moderate). Crossing structures were used by mammals and a large snake (moderate); measured effects rested on single spatial comparisons (very low). No study reported a human health outcome, and fire, landslides and water quality were unmeasured. Conclusions Roads act on these forests at two scales: kilometers for access-driven clearing, and tens to hundreds of meters for edge, mortality and barrier effects. Assessment boundaries and mitigation should match each mechanism’s scale, and mitigation

papers.title: Geomorphological Characteristics Based on Morphography, Morphometry, and Geomorphic Processes of the Silungkang Area, Sawahlunto City, West Sumatra
papers.summary: Geomorphology provides essential information on landscape evolution through the analysis of landforms, surface processes, and their controlling factors. This study was conducted in the Silungkang area and its surroundings, Sawahlunto City, West Sumatra, which lies within the Ombilin Basin, an intramontane basin interpreted as an oblique-rift to pull-apart basin associated with the Sumatra Fault System. The objective of this research is to identify and classify the geomorphology of the study area through morphographic, morphometric, and geomorphic-process analyses, and to delineate the landform units that compose it. The method integrates primary field observation with secondary interpretation of the National Digital Elevation Model (DEMNas), and the landform units were delineated using established genetic landform-classification schemes. The results show that the area is dominated by hills (about 70%), with elevations ranging from 185.49 to 873.29 m and slopes spanning flat (0–2%) to very steep (56–140%). Two main drainage patterns developed: subdendritic (62%) and dendritic (38%), while debris flow and debris slide are the observed mass movements. Based on the integration of these parameters, eleven landform units were identified, ranging from fluvial plains to denudational, karst, and intrusive hills. These units demonstrate that the landscape evolution of the study area is controlled by the combination of lithology, tectonic activity, and exogenic processes of weathering and erosion.

papers.title: Level of awareness and practices of the barangay officials towards disaster risk reduction and management in San Vicente, Palawan, Philippines
papers.summary: Barangay officials have a significant role in local disaster management in the Philippines, where natural hazards such as typhoons frequently occur. This study assessed the level of awareness and practices of barangay officials towards disaster risk reduction and management (DRRM). A descriptive-correlational research design was employed using a structured questionnaire. Gathered data from a total of 75 barangay officials in San Vicente, Palawan were analyzed using descriptive statistics and correlation tests. The results found that most of the respondents are male 53%, with ages between 39-48 years old, have attained college level education, a long-term resident of San Vicente, and had more than six years in government service. The respondents have identified typhoons, flooding, and landslides as the most common disasters experienced within the municipality. Results also revealed that the barangay officials showed high awareness particularly in search and rescue operations, their roles in DRRM, and designated evacuation centers. They also showed regular participation in DRRM activities, specifically training on first aid, search and rescue, and disaster management and information dissemination. However, they identified lack of training, lack of funds, and low community participation as the primary challenges to DRRM implementation. Moreover, results showed that there was no significant correlation between demographic profile and awareness, but disaster experience and DRRM practices did. These findings suggest that prior disaster experiences increase awareness, which in turn increases DRRM involvement. Though, barangay-level DRRM implementation necessitate institutional, financial, and participatory improvements.

Landslide‐Channel Coupling Controls Asymmetric Flash Flood—Debris Flow Transitions: Insights From an Extreme Rainfall‐Induced Hazard Chain in Yuzhong of China in 2025
papers.summary: Abstract Extreme rainfall‐triggered landslide–flash flood–debris flow hazard chains (LFFDF) are increasingly responsible for hydroclimatic losses worldwide. Although dynamics of individual hazards are established, transition mechanisms within LFFDF governed by coupled landslide–channel responses remain unresolved. Taking a catastrophic LFFDF event in northwestern China in 2025, we reconstructed the transition dynamics of the hazard chain using satellite data, seismic records, and numerical modeling. The results show that the LFFDF cascade operates as asymmetric transition processes, in which the dominant controls are state‐dependent. Rainfall‐induced landslides supplied one‐third of the mobilized sediment; their interaction with flash floods increased channel‐flow Shields stress by more than an order of magnitude, prematurely initiating debris flows in headwater channels. The downstream reversion from debris flow to flash flood is mainly controlled by the thickness and saturation state of channel sediments. Finally, we suggest a cascade‐based paradigm for risk assessment to enhance community resilience to LFFDF risks.

papers.title: Erosion-induced momentum production and system acceleration govern landslide mobility
papers.summary: Erosion can fundamentally alter landslide acceleration through the produced momentum. However, existing analytical landslide velocity models do not account for the energy dissipation associated with erosion-induced system acceleration. Here, I present a novel, complete dynamical velocity model for erosive landslides that incorporates two intrinsically coupled mechanically essential processes: erosion-induced acceleration and mobility booster through the net momentum production. This coupling is established analytically by formulating a simple equation for landslide velocity with erosion and deriving its elegant exact solution. I demonstrate that these two processes jointly govern the mobility of erosive landslides. My model applies to both non-deformable and deformable landslides, a key advantage, as erosive landslides are inherently deformable. The newly introduced booster velocity, defined as the ratio of erosion-induced acceleration to the mobility booster rate, provides the first precise mechanical criterion for determining landslide mobility: the lower the booster velocity, the higher the landslide mobility, a phenomenal understanding. This criterion incorporates all governing mechanisms: erosion rate, energy generator, and resulting acceleration. Remarkably, this result becomes possible only when erosion-induced acceleration is considered. However, contrary to prevailing perceptions, erosion-rate alone is insufficient to determine landslide mobility, irrespective of its magnitude. The model ascertains that accurate simulation of landslide dynamics requires accounting for erosion-induced reductions in frictional energy dissipation and inertia, alongside system acceleration, as these mechanisms collectively control landslide mobility. Neglecting erosion-induced reduced-inertia leads to physically inconsistent predictions and can substantially underestimate landslide mobility, potentially resulting in catastrophic consequences for people and infrastructure in lan

papers.title: A multi-source quantitative reconstruction of the 26 August 2026 Bhote Koshi rock-ice avalanche-debris-flow-flood cascade, Nepal
papers.summary: On 26 August 2026, a catastrophic transboundary mass-flow and flood cascade originated in the upper Lhende Khola-Bhote Koshi headwaters and propagated through the Bhote Koshi, Trishuli, and Narayani river system in Nepal. Early public descriptions used the glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) label, but subsequent seismic, satellite, video, field, hydrological, and damage-assessment evidence supported a more complex sequence of rock-ice avalanche, progressive entrainment and debris-flow transformation, followed by downstream flood-wave routing. This study aims to provide a reproducible, evidence-weighted quantitative reconstruction using publicly available data through 7 October 2026. Official hydrometeorological timelines, peer-reviewed source-process studies, preliminary satellite mapping, the Government of Nepal Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment, and dated human-impact snapshots were harmonized. Propagation and warning-time metrics, hydrological amplification, paired channel-width change at 22 sections, exposure and infrastructure severity ratios, and sectoral concentration of disaster effects and recovery needs were calculated. The source-to-border segment was reported at approximately 188 km/h (52.2 m/s), declining to 23-26 km/h in lower-river segments which was explained by a descriptive log-linear decay model at 80.1% of variation across six reported segment speeds. The public-warning anchor at 09:15 Nepal Standard Time occurred 38 minutes after the source seismic signal, after the flood had already passed or disabled upper-corridor stations, leaving only five minutes to the Betrawati station-failure proxy but 365 minutes to the reported Devghat flood-wave arrival. At Devghat, stage rose from 4.76 to 6.57 m, and discharge increased from approximately 2,600 to 5,850 m3/s where the reported 19.96 million m3 excess volume represented 34.8% of total flow volume during 14:10-18:00. papers.title: Contrasting slope histories under similar final-window rainfall in rock-slope failures: implications for monitoring
papers.summary: Rainfall is central to slope-hazard assessment and early warning, yet the meteorological state at release may not represent the pre-failure history of a rock slope. We reconstructed failure time, rolling precipitation windows, antecedent forcing, and precursor evidence for a purposively selected set of 12 natural rock-slope failures with resolvable event timing and meteorological evidence. Six events provided quantitative event-window rainfall: five had P24 = 0 mm and Pengshui had P24 = 0.9 mm. A sensitivity check across 12-, 24-, 48-, and 72-h windows showed that earlier rainfall re-entered the longer windows for some events, confirming that P24 is a standardized immediate descriptor rather than a trigger threshold. Within the six quantitative cases, antecedent histories ranged from multi-week dryness to earlier extreme rainfall, reservoir-level cycling, and short-lag rainfall, while documented precursor evidence ranged from multi-week deformation to minute-scale block shedding. Six additional boundary cases separated physical-process boundaries from evidence-definition boundaries. Because the search and retention criteria intentionally favored events with resolvable timing and meteorology, the set is not representative and is not used to estimate prevalence. The event-level comparison instead shows that a weak or absent final rainfall signal can coexist with contrasting pre-failure histories and monitoring evidence.

papers.title: The 7 April 2026 Reactivation of the Petacciato Landslide (Adriatic Coast, Italy): Field Evidence, Ground Deformation, and Rainfall-Triggering Conditions
papers.summary: The Petacciato landslide is a well-known, very large landslide located along the Adriatic coast of central–southern Italy and involving Plio-Pleistocene marine clay sequences with sandy intercalations. Reactivations have been documented since the early twentieth century and have occurred predominantly after prolonged rainfall periods. On 7 April 2026, a new reactivation event provided an opportunity to investigate this complex landslide system further. Displacements affected the A14 motorway and the Adriatic railway and led to the declaration of a national state of emergency. This study integrates geological, geomorphological, and hydrological information with recent European Ground Motion Service (EGMS) remote-sensing data and precipitation analyses to improve the understanding of the phenomenon. The findings indicate that the Apennine thrust front acts as a structural predisposing factor for the deep-seated landslide, whereas prolonged rainfall triggers reactivation. The analysis highlights the role of long-term cumulative rainfall as a primary driver of reactivation and the value of InSAR monitoring for evaluating continuous ground deformation, including during apparently dormant periods. The results emphasise how reactivation events can improve understanding of landslide behaviour and inform risk-management strategies.

papers.title: Emergency-Oriented Multi-Satellite SAR Incremental Replanning Using Multi-Relational Graph Convolution and Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization
papers.summary: Floods, earthquakes, and landslides may require a multi-satellite synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system to insert new observations after a regular plan has been prepared but before upload. The revised plan must respect visibility, imaging chronology, look-direction switching, orbit resources, strip formation, and plan stability. We propose a multi-relational graph convolutional network with constrained proximal policy optimization (GCN-PPO). Five opportunity relations encode conflict, feasible sequence, cross-satellite competition, demand alternatives, and strip synergy. A three-level policy selects the action category, logical completion unit, and observation opportunity, while feasibility-normalized constraints regulate emergency-service shortfall and plan perturbation. In a 300 s equal-budget experiment, all 750 returned schedules were feasible and free of hard-constraint violations, and 96.4% passed the preregistered timing contract. Under natural termination, GCN-PPO responded in 102.4 s on average, 9.35% of the ALNS time, and met the normalized emergency target in 98.1% of evaluations. Its per-edit perturbation was 31.4% lower than MLP-PPO and 35.9% lower than ALNS. Timely executable schedules support rapid SAR data acquisition for downstream disaster-object detection and emergency monitoring.

papers.title: How Much Sensing is Enough? Landslide Detection from Sparse and Noisy 3D Observations
papers.summary: Dense 3D terrain information is critical for accurate landslide detection; however, acquiring such data at large scale is often limited by sensing infrastructure, coverage, and environmental conditions. Emerging sensing modalities (e.g., mmWave, low-cost radar, sparse LiDAR) can operate under adverse conditions, but inherently produce sparse and noisy 3D observations, raising an important question: \emph{how much sensing is sufficient for reliable landslide detection?} Given the absence of large-scale sparse-terrain datasets, we have constructed a physics-informed dataset by combining digital elevation models from OpenTopography with soil moisture data from NASA's SMAP. Subsequently, we have randomly generated landslide events and introduced controlled sparsification and stochastic noise to emulate sensing constraints. We have then developed a learning-based framework to reconstruct the underlying terrain and identify landslide-prone regions using a CNN + XGBoost method. Our results show that with only 20\% of the original observations, the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 80\% and a ROC-AUC of 0.868, with a reconstruction error (L2 Chamfer Distance) of 99.67~$m^2$ on the test set. We have further studied the impact of sparsity, highlighting the trade-off between sensing density and detection performance.

papers.title: Methods and Tools for Multi-hazard Risk Assessment
papers.summary: Abstract Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment (MHRA) integrates hazard, exposure, and vulnerability analyses to quantify potential disaster impacts and support risk-informed decision-making. It evaluates the probability and consequences of multiple, interacting hazards such as floods, earthquakes, hurricanes, and landslides, and their cascading effects on people, infrastructure, and ecosystems. MHRA approaches range from qualitative methods, including community-based assessments and indicator-based analyses, to quantitative and probabilistic models that estimate economic and human losses. Advances in data availability, modelling, and artificial intelligence have enhanced the precision of risk estimation, while frameworks such as CAPRA, HAZUS, RiskScape, and CLIMADA provide practical tools for implementation. The chapter also highlights the importance of regional collaboration, uncertainty analysis, and scenario-based forecasting for adaptive planning. Strengthening MHRA capacities, particularly in data integration and multi-scale modelling, is essential to improving disaster preparedness, financial resilience, and long-term climate adaptation strategies.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Disaster Risk Management
authors: Marc J. C. Van den Homberg
papers.summary: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming disaster risk reduction and management by enhancing prediction, preparedness, response, and recovery. Leveraging techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, and foundation models, AI can analyse diverse datasets, including satellite imagery, sensor networks, social media, and historical disaster records, to improve early warning systems and risk assessments. AI applications range from predictive modelling of floods, earthquakes, landslides, and tropical cyclones to real-time damage assessment using computer vision and drones, and optimised emergency response planning. Additionally, AI supports post-disaster reconstruction and long-term recovery through economic modelling, infrastructure planning, and psychological support. Despite these benefits, challenges such as data scarcity, algorithmic bias, privacy concerns, and infrastructure requirements must be addressed to ensure equitable and effective deployment. Incorporating ethical frameworks, community engagement, and transparency is essential for maximising AI’s potential in building resilient communities and mitigating the social, economical, and environmental impacts of disasters.

papers.title: Massive debris flow activity and connectivity shift in the 1980s deciphered by combined terrestrial and lacustrine record in a changing climate
papers.summary: Abstract. Recent climatic change affects sediment transfer in Alpine catchments beyond historical experience, increasing the need for robust quantification of sediment cascades to better anticipate the frequency and magnitude of future climate-driven natural hazards. Despite widespread projections of increased natural hazard activity, many studies lack quantitative volume estimates over more than a decade. Lake Plansee, located in the Northern Calcareous Alps (Tyrol, Austria), represents a quasi-closed geomorphological system in which previous studies have identified an increase in debris flow activity since the 1920s. Here, we revisit historical aerial imagery using recent photogrammetric techniques to quantify sediment transfer on 54 debris fans to the lake between 1952 and 2020, and to establish a first-order quantitative reconciliation between terrestrial sediment-transfer estimates and sediment accumulation inferred from the lacustrine sink archive within a common source-to-sink framework. Fans surrounding Plansee are grouped based on their connection to the lake inferred from the co-occurrence of active channel linkage to the lake and net sediment export (i.e., negative net change). Twenty-one debris flow channels are connected to the lake and actively deliver sediment. Sixteen channels indicate progression towards the lake and are expected to connect in the future. Rainstorm intensity analysis shows that, since 1980, the number of days with precipitation intensities capable of initiating debris flows (>10 mm h-1) has increased by 36%, accompanied by a 12% increase in total erosion volumes and a 47% decrease in deposition volume at connected fans, suggesting an overall decrease in internal storage at the fans and enhanced sediment transport to the lake. The decadal response of sediment dynamics on the fans suggests that the increase in precipitation events results in an overall increase in sediment connectivity between catchments, fans, and the lake, driven by

papers.title: Date-Divergent reorganisation of soil organic and inorganic carbon pools during vegetation recovery at alpine landslide sites on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau
Supplementary material to "Thermokarst Domains of Canada"
Reply on RC2
papers.summary: Abstract. Geo-hydrological hazards, including floods and landslides, are among the most widespread hazards and a major cause of human loss worldwide. Their impacts are shaped by meteorological forcing and by long-term changes in exposure, vulnerability, and settlement patterns. Yet robust assessments of long-term fatality trends are rare because sufficiently long, accurate, and homogeneous records of damaging events are lacking. A key unresolved question is whether the human toll of geo-hydrological events has changed structurally through time, and which climatic, socio-economic, or policy factors best explain that change. Here we show, using a unique 1950–2024 catalogue of fatal events in Italy, that geo-hydrological risk underwent a marked transition, with fatalities and fatal days declining sharply until about 1970 and then stabilising at much lower levels. This decline was driven mainly by landslides, whereas flood-related losses showed weaker long-term change. The decline was not explained by specific risk policies or management programmes, as most of it preceded their implementation. Instead, precipitation was the main climatic driver of the remaining interannual variability, particularly for floods and days with fatal events. By contrast, population and gross domestic product did not account for the long-term trends once shared temporal changes were considered. Fatal days were less overdispersed and more predictable than fatalities, suggesting that meteorological factors control more directly the occurrence of dangerous conditions than the final death toll. Fatalities, instead, depend strongly on exposure, vulnerability, timing, location, and other event-specific circumstances. Together, these findings indicate that broad socio-economic dynamics can reduce geo-hydrological mortality even as hazardous processes persist, whereas meteo-climatic conditions continue to shape year-to-year risk.

papers.title: ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR ECONOMIC LOSSES DUE TO LANDSLIDES ON THE DIENG PLATEAU FOREST AREA
papers.summary: The Dieng Plateau is an area known for its agricultural cultivation. However, excessive use of land for agriculture increases the potential for landslides that disrupt community activities. This research aims to determine the potential losses due to landslides on agricultural land and determine strategies for managing environmental damage due to landslides in the Dieng Plateau. Determination of sample locations was carried out using the purposive sampling method, while data collection used the accidental sampling method. Data analysis uses quantitative techniques and SWOT analysis is used to formulate environmental damage management strategies. The research results show that the greatest losses due to landslides occur during the harvest period. The observation location that has the greatest potential for loss is location 1 which is Dieng Kulon Village. As the years go by, the resulting losses will be greater. The appropriate environmental management strategy to implement is Planting of vegetation types that are beneficial for the environment, tourism and agriculture to improve environmental quality and improve community welfare, stricter monitoring of agricultural activities, and the formation of a disaster response team.

papers.title: Asynchronous Hysteresis Rupture and Rheological Phase Transition in Anisotropic Porous Media Under Extreme Hydro-Climatic Forcing
papers.source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.summary: This paper presents a non-linear coupled hydromechanical framework governing the rheological phase transition and asynchronous hysteresis rupture in cohesive anisotropic porous media subjected to extreme hydro-climatic forcing. Traditional landslide susceptibility models and conventional finite element analyses (FEA) assume static geometric linearity, failing to capture non-associated plastic flow and spatial non-orthogonality under transience. To address this, we formalize the exact mathematical bifurcation point where the specific moisture capacity loses its protective bilinear nature due to state memory saturation, transferring incremental hydrostatic energy directly to the solid skeleton. The inception of static liquefaction and accelerated non-linear creep is mathematically constrained by the loss of ellipticity in the governing partial differential equations, analytically derived via the sub-determination of the elastoplastic acoustic tensor determinant det(Aik) <= 0. The theoretical thresholds established herein provide the closed-form mathematical baseline validated via the proprietary Project Zeus conceptual engine for early warning systems in critical geostructural infrastructure. For enterprise API licensing, early warning system integration, and commercial geostructural assessment, contact the Project Zeus Technical Despacho at carlos.gallo@cronoviaje.com

papers.title: Diagnosis and causal-chain-based treatment of water-leakage in in-service mountainous highway tunnels: an engineering application
papers.summary: Water leakage in in-service mountainous highway tunnels is difficult to diagnose due to concealed geological conditions, coupled seepage processes, and frequent recurrence after local repair. This study proposes a causal-diagnosis and causal-chain-based treatment framework for tunnel water leakage. The water-leakage mechanism is interpreted as a progressive process involving groundwater recharge, fracture-controlled seepage transport, drainage obstruction, water-pressure accumulation behind the lining, and failure at weak points in the waterproofing system. A diagnostic method integrating leakage characteristics, groundwater conditions, geological anomalies behind the lining, drainage performance, and waterproofing defects is established, followed by a three-stage treatment strategy. The framework was applied to the Dashiling Tunnel on the Shenzhen–Cenxi Expressway (G2518), China, using leakage surveys, seismic reflection imaging, and visual inspections. A total of 312 leakage defects were identified, with 48.1% occurring at secondary-lining construction joints and 37.8% occurring in wall-foot-to-sidewall zones. Fracture-related anomalies behind the lining and severe blockage in 50.0% of the inspected side drains revealed a compound leakage mechanism. After targeted treatment, two years of monitoring showed that the total area of pavement leakage was reduced to approximately 3.9% of its pre-treatment level. The number of tunnel water-leakage defects exhibited an approximately linear decreasing trend, with an overall reduction of more than 70%. The densities of tunnel water-leakage defects in all statistical sections were less than 0.3 points per linear meter, demonstrating good treatment effectiveness. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for the systematic diagnosis and treatment of water leakage in comparable in-service mountainous highway tunnels with similar hydrogeological and drainage conditions.

papers.title: ANALISIS POTENSI BENCANA LONGSOR DESA ORO-ORO OMBO BERDASARKAN KESESUAIAN RENCANA TATA RUANG WILAYAHKOTA BATU TAHUN 2010-2030
papers.source: Indonesian Journal of Environment and Disaster
papers.summary: Analysis of Landslide Hazard Potential in Oro-Oro Ombo Village Based on the Conformity with the Batu City Spatial Plan (2010–2030) This study aim to landslide-prone zones, their conformity with the Batu City Spatial Plan 2010–2030, and community preparedness. A mixed-method approach was used, combining quantitative spatial analysis based on a geographic information system with field observation, interviews, and documentation. The sample was purposively selected from high-hazard locations and areas of land-use mismatch, complemented by 27 informants from the village government and community for field validation. Hazard levels were determined by weighting five parameters: rainfall (30%), geology (20%), soil type (20%), land use (15%), and slope gradient (15%). Results showed that most of the village fell within moderate (227.99 ha), high (144.85 ha), and very high (78.04 ha) hazard categories, while low-hazard areas covered only 4.28 ha. About 28.22% of the area was inconsistent with the spatial plan, mainly residential and tourism zones within high to very high hazard areas, and two active landslide points were found near a residential area and a riverbank. Most respondents (78%) had never received disaster socialization, and although 56% were aware of evacuation routes, overall preparedness remained low due to limited structured disaster education. This study recommends stricter spatial use controls, structural mitigation, and enhanced disaster education.

papers.title: Pengaruh Pembelajaran Mitigasi Bencana Tanah Longsor Terhadap Peningkatan Pengetahuan Siswa
papers.source: Indonesian Journal of Environment and Disaster
papers.summary: The Effect of Landslide Mitigation Education on Increasing Students' Knowledge Indonesia is a country that is vulnerable to various natural disasters, including hydrometeorological disasters such as landslides, which often cause environmental, social, and economic losses, especially in mountainous areas with high rainfall. Therefore, disaster mitigation education is important to improve community preparedness, including among elementary school students. One effort that can be implemented is the use of innovative learning media such as animated videos that present material in an audio-visual form, making it more interesting and easier for students to understand. This study aims to determine the effect of using animated video media on increasing the knowledge of fourth-grade students at SD Negeri 1 Sukawana regarding landslide disaster mitigation. The study used a quantitative approach with a pretest and posttest method. The results of the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test showed a significance value of 0.000, indicating that the data were not normally distributed; therefore, the analysis was continued using the Wilcoxon test. The Wilcoxon test results showed a significance value of 0.000 (<0.05), indicating a significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores. Thus, animated video media has proven to be effective in improving students' knowledge.

papers.title: AN EVALUATION OF COMMUNITY KNOWLEDGE LEVEL ON SPATIAL UTILIZATION IN LANDSLIDE PRONE AREAS IN NGARGOYOSO SUB DISTRICT YEAR 2025
papers.source: Indonesian Journal of Environment and Disaster
papers.summary: Land-use change in Ngargoyoso District has increased due to tourism expansion. Situated on Mount Lawu's slopes with high landslide susceptibility, improper spatial utilization and low public understanding of Spatial Planning escalate disaster risks. This study aims to analyze public knowledge levels regarding spatial utilization in landslide-prone areas and its influencing factors in 2025. The research employs a descriptive quantitative approach supported by explicit qualitative data. Primary data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with 99 heads of households selected via stratified random sampling. Qualitative data occupies an explicit position to contextualize quantitative findings, analyzed using the Miles & Huberman (1994) model. Results show public knowledge is generally low (80.8%), with Segorogunung and Jatirejo Villages in the moderate category. Factors such as education, licensing experience, and socialization access significantly influence knowledge levels. This research provides a scientific contribution by integrating spatial literacy into community-based disaster risk reduction, emphasizing that vulnerability is determined by both physical factors and legal-spatial understanding. It underscores the need for strengthened education and participatory supervision in spatial utilization.

papers.title: PEMETAAN KERAWANAN TANAH LONGSOR MENGGUNAKAN METODE FREQUENCY RATIO BERBASIS SIG DI KOTA BATU
papers.source: Indonesian Journal of Environment and Disaster
papers.summary: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using the Frequency Ratio Method Based on Geographic Information Systems in Batu City This study aimed to analyze the level of landslide susceptibility in Batu City using the Frequency Ratio (FR) method based on Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The analysis was carried out using nine conditioning parameters, and the results showed that four main factors had the most significant influence: slope steepness, rainfall intensity, elevation, and soil type. All data were processed in 30-meter resolution raster format using pixel-based spatial analysis. The results indicated that areas with steep slopes, rainfall exceeding 3000 mm per year, elevations above 1500 meters above sea level, and Andosol soil types had the highest levels of landslide susceptibility. The northern part of Batu City, particularly Bumiaji District, was identified as the most vulnerable area, followed by Batu District, while Junrejo District had the lowest susceptibility level. Model validation using the Kappa coefficient produced a value of 0.70 with an overall accuracy of 85%, indicating that the FR model was reliable in representing the spatial distribution of landslide susceptibility. The findings of this study are expected to serve as a reference for disaster mitigation efforts and spatial planning in Batu City.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Environment-Based Augmented Reality Media on Junior High Students’ Disaster Mitigation Literacy
papers.summary: This study investigated the effectiveness of local environment-based Augmented Reality (AR) media in improving junior high school students’ disaster mitigation literacy. The AR media integrated Pacitan Regency’s local environmental context and disaster-related topics, including forest conservation, floods, and landslides, into Grade VII ecology and biodiversity learning. A quantitative approach with a one-group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental design was employed. The intervention was implemented by junior high school science teachers in Pacitan Regency and involved 209 Grade VII students. Disaster mitigation literacy data were collected using pretest and posttest instruments and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Normalized Gain (N-Gain), the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test, the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, and effect size analysis. The mean score increased from 78.30 (pretest) to 93.95 (posttest), with a high average N-Gain of 0.76. The Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test indicated a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (p < 0.001), while the effect size (r = 0.85) demonstrated a strong educational impact. These findings indicate that local environment-based AR media effectively enhances disaster mitigation literacy by providing contextual, interactive, and meaningful learning experiences for students in disaster-prone areas.

papers.title: LeMoRe-MTKD: A Multi-Teacher–Student Knowledge Distillation Deep Learning Framework for Landslide Segmentation Using UAV Imagery
papers.summary: Landslides (LSs) are a natural phenomenon, typically triggered by heavy rainfall and earthquakes, and pose a global danger to human lives and property. LSs frequently occur on steep slopes and in loose soil conditions, and damaged sites can be hard to reach thereafter. Thus, remote approaches would be relevant and practical for investigations, and the use of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) for imaging, along with robust methods to identify and quantify LS-affected areas, is recommended. Therefore, this study proposed a multi-teacher–student knowledge distillation (KD) deep learning framework for landslide semantic segmentation. The lightweight LeMoRe model is selected for the learner model (student), and SegNet, U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and LinkNet are used as the teacher networks. To establish the UAV training dataset, we conducted UAV imaging for four LS sites, including Mogo, Buri, Oejeong, and Sangneung (testing site) villages, in Sancheong County, South Korea, in 2025. First, all plain networks are trained on the training dataset, and then KD is applied for single-teacher and multi-teacher KD. Subsequently, ablation studies are implemented to identify the optimal KD component set and the best student–teacher combination (with equal weights) for subsequent experiments. In addition, the equal-weight combination is tuned for the optimal teacher weight proportion to maximize the teacher knowledge transfer to the student. The best model weight is saved for inference with the testing site of Sangneung to map the LS-damaged areas. The experiment results reveal an improvement in accuracy (6.3% F1, 8.2% IoU with equal weight and 12.3% F1 and around 16.8% IoU with the tuned weight). The inference results for the Sangneung testing site were qualitatively and quantitatively evaluated through visual comparison with the original UAV imagery with three zoom-in areas presented for detailed examination. Finally, efficiency, the trade-off between accuracy and efficiency, limitations,

papers.title: Rapid formation of meter-scale ripples on modern Mars
Emerging trends in AI-driven mining hazard management
papers.summary: The management of geotechnical hazards in mining is critical for ensuring operational safety and sustainability, yet its practical implementation often struggles with the inherent geological uncertainty and the dynamic, non-linear nature of mining environments. Artificial intelligence (AI), and specifically machine learning (ML), has emerged as a transformative technology, offering a shift from reactive to proactive, data-driven hazard management. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the evolution and application of AI in mining hazard management, tracing this development from early statistical and ML models to recent advances in deep learning. The review finds that these advanced models have demonstrated significant success in tasks such as rockburst prediction, slope stability analysis, and gas outburst forecasting by identifying complex patterns in large, multi-source datasets from seismic, geological, and operational monitoring. Despite these successes, significant challenges persist: the efficacy of purely data-driven models is often limited by data scarcity, imbalanced datasets, and a lack of physical consistency; the black-box nature of many deep learning models has created a barrier to their interpretability and trustworthiness in safety-critical applications. The future of AI in mining hazard management lies not in isolated algorithms but in integrated, hybrid systems. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and explainable AI (XAI) are identified as critical frontiers. These approaches promise to create models that are not only more accurate and generalisable but also transparent and interpretable to engineering practitioners, bridging the gap between AI's theoretical potential and its practical application in creating safer mining environments.

papers.title: Northern Colombian Andes Database: Hillslope Torrential Cascade (HTC) Inventory and Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) Tracking
papers.source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.summary: This repository contains a comprehensive geospatial and climatological database for investigating hillslope torrential cascades (HTCs) and mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) in the northern Colombian Andes. The repository was originally developed to support a first study focused exclusively on the climatology, detection, tracking, and spatiotemporal characterization of MCSs. The present version extends that original atmospheric database to support a second study integrating organized convective exposure with a regional inventory of hillslope torrential cascades and associated geomorphic and environmental characteristics. The repository therefore preserves the continuity of the MCS analysis while incorporating the additional geomorphic information required to investigate the spatial correspondence between terrain predisposition and organized convection. The MCS component contains the detection, tracking, and characterization of mesoscale convective systems over the northern Andean region for the climatological period analyzed in the associated studies. MCS trajectories were generated using the Algorithm for TRACKing Convective Systems (ATRACKCS) following the methodological framework of Robledo et al. (2024). The tracking database was derived from satellite-based precipitation estimates from GPM IMERG and infrared brightness-temperature observations from NOAA/NCEP-CPC MERGE IR, using detection and tracking criteria consistent with those adopted for northwestern South America. The resulting products include MCS trajectories and derived spatial, temporal, lifecycle, precipitation, and kinematic diagnostics used in the associated analyses. The HTC component, incorporated for the second study, contains a multi-temporal regional inventory of hillslope torrential cascade environments and shallow-landslide swarms across the northern Colombian Andes. The inventory integrates mapped observations from satellite and remote-sensing imagery together with geomorphic, morphometric

papers.title: Reproducibility archive for a leave-one-county-out evaluation of spatial leakage in object-centric landslide detection
papers.source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.summary: Spatial Leakage in Object-Centric Landslide Detection Reproducibility package for a leave-one-county-out (LOCO) evaluation of spatial leakage in object-centric (bounding-box) landslide detection on the Bijie landslide benchmark. The question this package addresses: **how large is the apparent accuracy advantage obtained when training and testing patches are drawn randomly from the same region, and how much of that advantage depends on which evaluation metric is reported?** Citation Yongzhu Xiong, Mingyong Zhu, Youcun Liu, Haifeng Huang. (a) School of Geography and Tourism, Jiaying University, Meizhou, Guangdong, China(b) National Field Observation and Research Station of Landslides in the Three Gorges Reservoir Area of the Yangtze River, China Three Gorges University, Yichang 443002, Hubei, China The Bijie landslide dataset is used under courtesy of its original providers.

papers.title: Delphi-Based Prioritization of Climate and Weather- Related Risks and Their Time-Cost-Quality-Safety Effects on Public Infrastructure Projects in Leyte, Philippines
papers.summary: Climate and weather-related hazards pose significant challenges to infrastructure project implementation in Leyte Province, Philippines, where typhoons, heavy rainfall, flooding, landslides, and coastal hazards can disrupt construction activities and affect project performance. This study aimed to identify, assess, and prioritize climate and weather-related risks affecting public infrastructure projects in Leyte Province and to determine their effects on project time, cost, quality, and safety. A three-round Delphi study was conducted with 18 infrastructure professionals, all of whom participated in each round. Round 1 focused on risk identification, while Rounds 2 and 3 assessed and validated the frequency and severity of the identified risks using a five-point Likert scale. Frequency Index, Severity Index, and Importance Index were used to assess and prioritize the risks, while Pareto Analysis was applied to determine their cumulative contribution to the overall risk profile. The Kruskal–Wallis test was used to examine differences in expert assessments across selected respondent characteristics. The study identified 49 climate and weather-related risks grouped into seven themes. The three highest-ranked risks were disruption of project logistics and material delivery during typhoon events (II = 0.693), delay or suspension of construction activities due to typhoon events (II = 0.667), and storm surge impacts on coastal infrastructure (II = 0.604). The TCQS assessment showed that these risks had varying effects on project performance, with logistics disruption having its strongest effects on cost and quality, while typhoon-related work suspension had its strongest effects on time and safety. Overall, the findings demonstrate that climate and weather-related risks should be explicitly considered in public infrastructure planning and construction management in Leyte Province, particularly in prioritizing risks and developing measures to minimize their effects on proje

papers.title: Influence of landslide inventory representation and land cover configuration on landslide susceptibility mapping: a comparative machine learning analysis from the Taslidere Catchment (Türkiye)
A review of submarine landslides in the Ischia Island offshore (Tyrrhenian Sea)
papers.summary: Abstract A revision of the submarine landslides occurring in the Ischia offshore has been carried out, considering theoretical approaches, modeling, and seismo-stratigraphic data, focusing on the Ischia Island example. Based on the literature data, marine hazards and tsunami assessment have been considered. Although sidescan sonar data demonstrating the hummocky facies in the northern Ischia offshore have not been published, morpho-bathymetric data from earlier studies have been reinterpreted. Only a portion of the seismo-stratigraphic data has been reevaluated, and newly interpreted seismic sections are displayed. Major debris-avalanche deposits are preserved in the offshore areas in the north, west, and south, whose chronostratigraphic age is Holocene. Deposits from Northern Ischia exhibit blocky acoustic facies and hummocky/mounded morphology. Multiple generations of mass-transport deposits are suggested by the geological interpretation of seismic profiles. The main implication for the hazard evaluation is highlighted by the presence of significant underwater deposits off the northern, western, and southern coasts, suggesting that Ischia is characterized by a marked susceptibility to landslides, some of which may have reached speeds that made them potentially tsunami-generating and a risk to the local population and infrastructure. The factor of safety has been evaluated based on literature data. With a factor of safety ranging from 2.01 to 3.69, the majority of coastal sectors exhibit extremely low levels. This is also true for Forio (western Ischia) and Casamicciola (northern Ischia), where significant debris avalanche deposits are found in the nearby offshore. This makes these locations less likely to slip. On the contrary, the southern part of Ischia has a very high factor of safety (less than 1.01), particularly in the Maronti and S. Angelo sectors, which may be vulnerable to slides. Seismic sections on Ischia’s southern slope, which exhibit significant slop

papers.title: Topographic controls on vegetation recovery in mass-movement scars after an extreme rainfall event in Southern Brazil
papers.summary: Abstract Understanding vegetation recovery in landslide scars is essential for risk assessment and post‑disaster management. This study investigated how geomorphometric attributes influence vegetation regeneration in 85 mass‑movement scars triggered by an extreme precipitation event in January 2017 in southern Brazil. Annual time series (2018–2026) of four Sentinel‑2 spectral indices were integrated with topographic variables derived from the Copernicus GLO‑30 DEM. Principal component analysis (PCA) and k-means clustering classified scars into high, medium, and low regeneration groups, while linear mixed models evaluated topographic effects on recovery trajectories. Results demonstrated that regeneration follows a non-linear temporal trajectory, characterized by rapid initial recovery followed by progressive leveling off, which is partly tied to optical index saturation limits in maturing canopies. Slope negatively affected vegetation moisture levels, and elevation significantly modulated the bare soil trajectory, with higher altitudes showing faster soil recovery rates. Scar shape, measured by the circularity index, did not exert a significant effect on any spectral index. Curvature and aspect did not significantly influence regeneration trajectories. The high-regeneration class represented 42.3% of the scars analyzed, indicating relatively greater spectral recovery in most areas, while steep, low‑elevation sites require targeted restoration to reduce erosion and landslide reactivation risk. These results demonstrate that geomorphometric attributes are associated with different dimensions of the observed spectral recovery trajectories and that the approach integrating multiple spectral indices and non-linear modeling is effective for identifying priority areas for long-term ecological monitoring, thereby supporting landslide risk mitigation in subtropical environments.

papers.title: Bobcat-rhinopithecus optimization for energy and trust aware cluster based routing in wireless sensor network
Climate-induced Displacement in Rwanda. Case Study of Landslides in Rutsiro District, Western Rwanda
Analysis of the Mapping Relationship Between Rock Infrared Emissivity and Brightness Temperature in Different Background Environments
papers.summary: The increase in thermal infrared brightness temperature and infrared emissivity observed during rock loading provides important insight into the physical mechanisms underlying thermal infrared anomalies associated with geological hazards, including earthquakes, landslides and rockbursts. However, the relationship between rock emissivity and brightness temperature is strongly influenced by the surrounding radiative environment, and how background radiation affects this relationship remains insufficiently understood. From the perspective of remote-sensing physics, this study investigates the influence of background radiation on the emissivity–brightness temperature relationship at the surfaces of multiple rock types. Experiments involving background-radiation measurements and rock-emissivity retrievals were conducted under different environmental conditions, and a physical relationship between background radiation and rock-surface brightness temperature was established. The results show that (1) the background radiation in the outdoor environment is mainly derived from the cold sky background, while the background radiation in the indoor environment tends to be close to the body radiation; and (2) in the indoor environment, the change in the emissivity is almost incapable of causing a brightness temperature response, and it is difficult to realize emissivity inversion, while in the outdoor environment, the mapping relationship between brightness temperature and emissivity is more relevant. Based on these findings, we developed an experimental configuration combining a movable chamber that opens to expose the loading platform to the sky with a multi-angle remote sensing observation loading platform designed to reduce structural obstruction. This configuration enables switching between enclosed and open-air conditions without relocating the loading platform and increases the contribution of cold sky background radiation to the radiation incident on the rock surface.
